 Order
With consent heard finally.

1. The present petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner seeking quashment of FIR registered at Police Station - Seondha, District Datia vide Crime No.88/2018 for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act and further consequential proceedings arising out of it,on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.

2. From perusal of facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that at the instance of the father of the prosecutrix a missing person's report was lodged on 31.07.2018 regarding missing of his daughter on 28.07.2018.
On the basis of such missing person's report, an FIR was registered for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC against the suspected petitioner.
Matter was investigated and prosecutrix was recovered.

Her statement under NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19483 2 MCRC-51313-2023 Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded.
After completion of investigation and other formalities, charge sheet was filed.
Now petitioner and prosecutrix married to each other and prosecutrix is living in her household peacefully.

sentences.text: Meanwhile, it appears that it is a case where both married to each other and entered into a wedlock and now, prosecutrix is living with her husband (petitioner).
Both the parties expressed their desire to settle the matter because petitioner and prosecutrix are living as married couple.
Therefore, this petition has been preferred under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashment of FIR as well as consequential criminal proceedings arising thereto.
4. This Court referred the matter before Principal Registrar of this Court for verification of factum of compromise.
Before the Principal Registrar of this Court, both the parties appeared and expressed their desire to settle their case.
Today also, both the parties wanted to settle the matter and they do not want to prosecute the case further.
5. A specific query being made by this Court and it was found that both the parties are living peacefully as married couple.
Petitioner/accused and respondent No.2/victim are also ready to bury the hatchet, if any.
6. Learned counsel for petitioner as well as respondent No.2/victim also advanced arguments in support of compounding of the case.
7. Counsel for the respondent/State opposed the prayer, however, could not dispute the facts, as submitted.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19483 3 MCRC-51313-2023 appended thereto.
9.
This is a case where petitioner and respondent No.2 shared emotional and physical proximity.

At the instance of father of prosecutrix, case was registered against petitioner, but statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. indicates that both the parties shared the proximity by mutual consent.
She left her maternal home on her on volition.

Although, at the relevant point of time,
prosecutrix was minor and was at the cusp of attaining majority because her age was around 17 years, but later on she attained majority and thereafter, prosecutrix and accused entered into a wedlock.

10. Although, it is the submission of learned counsel for the parties that petitioner and respondent No.2 are living together as married couple under one roof, now there is no dispute left between the petitioner and respondent No.2.
Both the parties earlier appeared before Principal Registrar of this Court on 25.10.2024 and expressed their desire for settlement.

11. Be that as it may.
12.
The fact remains that petitioner and respondent No.2 are married couple and both are living under one roof.
It is regular and easy to be retributive, but at the same time a Judge has to sublimely feel the pulse of the case.
One cannot forget that "Every "F I L E" with same alphabets, contains a "L I F E".

(See : In Re State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Pankaj Mishra, 2021 SCC OnLine MP 5480 and Geeta Paliwal and others Vs. Sitaram and others reported as 2023 SCC Online MP 811.)

Here "FILE" before this Court carries not only a "LIFE" but many NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19483 4 MCRC-51313-2023 LIVES.
14.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case I.A.No.16192/2024 is hereby allowed and parties are permitted to enter into compromise.

15. Therefore, this Court under the obtaining facts and circumstances of the case intends to tread on the path of reformative or at least other than retributive one because:-
(i) A girl of tender age around (16-17 years) has fallen in love with young boy and driven by hormones, they shared emotional and physical proximity and moved out of social/legal limits.
(ii) Girl was of consistent view that she shared emotional/physical proximity on her own volition and she left her maternal home voluntarily.
Her statements under Section 164 Cr.P.C. indicate so.
(iii) Petitioner and prosecutrix entered into a wedlock and girl/prosecutrix is living peacefully with the petitioner.
In case of any punishment, petitioner may have to go to jail and that would disrupt the family forever.
(iv) Today, they expressed their desire to settle the matter.
Therefore, in the cumulative facts and circumstances of the case, matter deserves consideration.
(v) Petitioner does not have any previous criminal background so as to infer any mischief at this juncture.

Therefore, keeping this spirit, this Court intends to inject "L I F E"
into this "F I L E" in the interest of justice.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19483 5 MCRC-51313-2023 16.

Resultantly, petition stands allowed and FIR No.88/2018 registered at PS- Seonda, District Datia for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act and further consequential proceedings arising out of it stand quashed.
Petitioner is set free.

But,
an expectation can certainly be raised by this Court that petitioner/accused and respondent No.2/prosecutrix shall live peacefully and would try to attain nuptial bliss so that family and social harmony can be maintained.
17. Petition stands allowed and disposed of.
(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
